question: Which of the following tests is used for starch detection?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine test**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **iodine test** is used for **starch detection** because iodine reacts with the starch molecules to form a blue-black color complex.
 
• The **glucose test** is used to detect the **presence of glucose** in a sample, not starch.
 
• **Starch** is a** complex carbohydrate **made up of glucose molecules.
 
• It is a common source of energy in many foods such as rice, potatoes, and bread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** glucose test** involves the use of a reagent such as **Benedict's solution**, which changes color in the presence of reducing sugars such as glucose.
 
• The **salt test **is a test used to check the **purity of a sample** by adding salt to the sample and observing any changes in the physical properties such as solubility or melting point.
 
• The **sodium test** is a test used to detect the presence of **sodium ions **in a sample.
 
 
• It involves the use of a reagent such as , which reacts with sodium ions to form a yellow precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Starch** is an important component of many foods and is a major source of energy for humans and animals.
 
 
• It is also used in many industrial applications such as** papermaking and textile manufacturing.**
